title: Final Parking Space: 1948 Kaiser Special

body_markdown:
Once the challenge of crushing the Axis was over, what was the[mighty industrialist](https://about.kaiserpermanente.org/who-we-are/our-history/henry-j-kaiser-americas-health-care-visionary) Henry J. Kaiser going to do to keep busy? *[Build cars](https://www.hagerty.com/media/archived/kaiser-frazer-went-down-swinging/)* , of course, and that’s[just what he did](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/kaiser-frazers-mid-century-family-cars-were-true-convertibles/) once the war ended. Today’s Final Parking Space subject is one of the early products of the Kaiser-Frazer Corporation, now residing in[a Denver self-service wrecking yard](https://www.upullandpay.com/locations/colorado/denver/) .


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


If you’re near the Mile High City and you go looking for parts from this car, be aware that U-Pull-&-Pay has it listed as a “1950 Miscellaneous Car,” because their data-entry system doesn’t have a place for Kaisers or Frazers. This sort of thing happens when older vehicles from defunct makes must be accounted for in a modern inventory-management system.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I’ve documented[a half-dozen or so Kaisers and Frazers in Colorado car graveyards](https://www.murileemartin.com/Junkyard/JunkyardGallery-AMC.html) over the years, including[this Horizon Blue ’49 Special](https://www.thetruthaboutcars.com/2012/08/junkyard-find-horizon-blue-1949-kaiser-special/) , and today’s car is one of the more solid ones.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Except for a small hole in the passenger footwell floor, I couldn’t find any rust-through in this car.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


In the trunk, I found a torn-off piece of a page from the Denver *Post* that I’m dating from about 1954, judging by the[“Slow Down and Live”](https://www.nytimes.com/1954/08/06/archives/drive-on-speeding-held-big-success-slowdownandlive-plea-is-hailed.html?unlocked_article_code=1.EFE.M9bt.NwDyjdgnw-e8&smid=url-share) driving-safety advertisement and the story about the horse-kicked daughter of a prominent Denver family.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Unlike most cars of this age that I find in junkyards, the interior of this one wasn’t particularly cluttered. There were some old Montgomery Ward’s spark plugs and not much dirt or rodent-nesting material.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I think this car was stored in a leaky but sun-protected shed or lean-to for a half-century or so, then pulled out with the idea of reviving it. The tires are fairly recent, suggesting they were put on to enable the car to be moved around a yard.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The cowl tag tells us that this car is a 1948 Special, originally painted in[Turf Green](https://circlekf.com/kfcars/KFCPDupont_490415.pdf) .


Kaiser-Frazer Corporation


Kaiser-Frazer offered two makes at first: Kaiser and Frazer. For the 1947-1950 model years (and into a bit of 1951, when 1950 Frazers were built to use up leftover parts inventory), Kaiser was the low-priced brand and Frazer was the luxury brand. The products of both makes were built on the same platform and looked similar to each other during this period. The Special was the cheapest Kaiser-Frazer car through 1950.


Kaiser-Frazer Corporation


Other than the slab sides (which looked modern next to the prewar designs being built by other manufacturers), there wasn’t much noteworthy about Kaiser-Frazer cars when the first 1947 models appeared in the summer of 1946. Fortunately for Kaiser-Frazer, *any* new car was sure to be bought by Americans with money to spend and an insatiable hunger for fresh wheels.


Kaiser-Frazer Corporation


The original Kaiser-Frazer plan, hatched in the summer of 1945 after Bank of America founder A.P. Giannini suggested that Henry Kaiser team up with experienced car-industry heavyweight Joseph Frazer, was to develop a technologically advanced low-priced car, possibly with front-wheel drive. The costs of starting a car company from scratch and creating products to compete with Ford, GM, and Chrysler in a hurry forced Kaiser and Frazer to throw out that idea, and they went with an entirely conventional design for their initial products.


Kaiser-Frazer Corporation


Kaisers and Frazers were well-built cars, but they were expensive for what the customers got. The cheapest possible 1947 Kaiser-Frazer, the Special, had a sticker price of $1868, or about $29,104 in 2026 dollars.


Chevrolet Division, General Motors


Meanwhile, GM offered the 1947 Chevrolet Stylemaster four-door sedan starting at a mere $1276 (about $19,881 after inflation). Sure, it looked painfully prewar, but so what? It was cheap, and it came from a trusted automotive brand.


Kaiser-Frazer Corporation


Perhaps Kaiser-Frazer’s biggest weak point lived under the hood. There was no way the company could have developed an all-new engine from scratch in a year, so they had to buy one. This turned out to be the 226-cubic-inch version of the venerable flathead straight-six family made by the Continental Motors Company. The Continental flathead six powered[a bewildering assortment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Motors_Company#Automobiles) of vehicles before World War II, including some made by Joe Frazer’s[Graham-Paige](https://oldcarbrochures.org/United%20States/Graham-Paige/1939-Graham/1939-Graham-Brochure/index.html) . It was a known quantity and got the job done, but that was about the best that could be said about it.


Checker Motors Corporation


The Continental 226 got the last laugh, though, because it was[the final valve-in-block engine](https://www.autoweek.com/car-life/a1713546/what-was-final-year-new-flathead-powered-american-car/) to be installed in a new American production car: the 1964 Checker. If you accept the Jeep DJ as a car and not a truck (I don’t), then the winner of the Final Flathead prize is the Go-Devil-powered[1965 Jeep DJ-3A](https://oldcarbrochures.com/static/NA/Jeep/1965%20Jeep/1965%20Jeep%20Full%20Line%20Brochure%20(R2)/index1.html) .


Kaiser-Frazer Corporation


At the same time, the costs of converting[the gigantic Willow Run bomber factory](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/watch-fords-willow-run-plant-churn-out-a-b-24-every-55-minutes/) into an automobile production plant were draining Kaiser-Frazer’s startup capital at an alarming rate. Friction between Henry Kaiser, the man who could build a Liberty Ship in under five days at one-quarter the cost of his rivals, and Joe Frazer, the veteran Detroit car-builder who[thought up the Plymouth brand name](https://bangshift.com/general-news/friday-fact-plymouth-car-company-named-brand-twine/) and[made the Jeep happen](https://richardlangworth.com/frazer-1) , got worse as Kaiser insisted on powering through all obstacles while Frazer pointed out the scary numbers on the ledger. It didn’t help Kaiser-Frazer that shortages of raw materials continued into the early postwar era and well-established Detroit competitors had the edge on connections with suppliers.


Kaiser-Frazer Corporation


For the 1947 and 1948 model years, neither antiquated engines nor big price tags mattered to wheels-crazed postwar American car shoppers, and Kaiser-Frazer sold every car it could build. Then 1949 hit and the Detroit behemoths introduced all-new modern designs while finally getting back up to full production capacity. If you wanted a new[’49 Ford](https://murileemartin.substack.com/p/reconstituted-junkyard-jewel-1949) , you could get one *right now* and the four-door sedan started at just $1472. The Kaiser Special listed at $1995.


Kaiser-Frazer Corporation


Joe Frazer had seen the problems of 1949 coming, but Henry Kaiser proved as stubborn as the buffalo depicted on his cars’ hood ornaments. After a failed stock offering in early 1948 and a tumultuous board meeting later that year, any meaningful role for Frazer in the company was over.


Kaiser-Frazer Corporation


The Kaiser-Frazer Corporation held on until 1953 and built some interesting products during its final years. After that, Kaiser bought Willys-Overland to create the Kaiser-Willys Corporation and went all-truck in the U.S. market after 1955; in 1963 the company was renamed Kaiser Jeep. Other than the Jeep brand, Henry J. Kaiser’s best-known legacy is[the healthcare company](https://about.kaiserpermanente.org/who-we-are/our-history) he founded in Oakland for his shipyard employees during World War II. For the complete story of Kaiser-Frazer, I suggest you read Aaron Severson’s exhaustive *Kaisers Never Retrench* article ([Part I](https://ateupwithmotor.com/model-histories/kaiser-frazer-part-1/view-all/) /[Part II](https://ateupwithmotor.com/model-histories/kaiser-frazer-part-2/view-all/) ).


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Now that the history lesson is over, we’ll take a closer look at this Special. It was born at Willow Run; the 8033rd Kaiser built out of 91,851 total for the 1948 model year. Its early production number suggests that it was being assembled right around the time of the escalating squabbles between Kaiser and Frazer and the unsuccessful stock offering.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The odometer shows just under 50,000 miles. If this car got parked for good in the middle 1950s, this could be the actual mileage.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


There’s a genuine Kaiser-Frazer “Air Conditioner” under the dash.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


However, that designation didn’t mean what it means today; this AC is just an optional heater/ventilator/defroster unit.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The inside door-latch releases use an interesting setup. You push the button to open the door, which makes accidental opening less likely than with the usual handles.


Kaiser-Frazer Corporation


The Frazer got the same rig, but with[the Frazer coat of arms](https://fineartamerica.com/featured/1948-kaiser-frazer-emblem-jill-reger.html) rather than the Kaiser buffalo on the button.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The engine was rated 100 horsepower; the[Frazer Manhattan](https://www.autoblog.com/features/junkyard-gem-1947-frazer-manhattan) came with a dual-carb version that made 112 horses.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Of the major low-priced American brands, only Chevrolet offered an overhead-valve engine for the 1948 model year. That would change soon enough.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The transmission is the mandatory three-speed column-shift manual. Frazers could be purchased with an optional overdrive unit.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


There are what appears to be a couple of blanket-and-plastic-wrapped cushions atop the original front bench.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Every driver knew the Fahrenheit boiling point of water in 1948. The Continental engine, like nearly all flatheads with their exhaust-through-the-block designs, was prone to overheating under load.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The body is exceptionally solid and much of the glass and interior trim is still intact. As restoration projects go, this one wouldn’t have been too difficult.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Unfortunately, no-frills postwar Detroit sedans just don’t get much love these days.


“Today, Kaiser-Frazer is the fourth-largest producer of automobiles in the world.”


Just like building Liberators five years ago!
